newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close slightly down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close slightly down in slow trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly down on Friday in slow trade amid a pre-holiday mood with many players staying on the sidelines, and brokers expected the inactive market sentiment to continue.
Some year-end profit-taking by institutional investors continued from Thursday, pulling the index down, though minor buying was seen in low-priced shares such as cements and textiles.
The weighted index slid 26.01 points or 0.38 percent to end at 6,863.02. Turnover was a small T$32 billion.
Brokers attributed the sluggish sentiment mainly to the approach of the end of this year.

"There is no market-inspiring news to stimulate investors and many people prefer to stay away from the market before the weekend and the upcoming new year holiday," said Foremost Invsetment analyst Wang Jieh.

As the index has failed to breach the psychological barrier of 7,000 points in the past few weeks, many brokers said the index might weaver below that barrier in the last three trading sessions in 1996.

"The domestic economy should turn better in 1997, so the current correction will not hurt the overall market optimism in the medium term," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities, noting a current economic recovery at home.
Buying interest would continue to focus on blue chips and low-priced shares though major movements in share prices were not likely, brokers said.
A 6,800-6,900 point trading range was expected in coming sessions. -- Joyce Liu (2-5080815)
